facts.text: BaslerCamera is the PyMoDAQ plugin's camera class and wraps one pylon.InstantCamera
open() attaches the pylon device, opens it and reads the per-model attribute configuration
get_roi returns x0, x0+width, y0, y0+height, xbin and ybin from the pylon OffsetX, Width, OffsetY, Height, BinningHorizontal and BinningVertical nodes
set_roi clamps the start and end coordinates to the detector size, aligns each start to Width.Inc and writes OffsetX, Width, OffsetY, Height, BinningHorizontal and BinningVertical
detector_clamp bounds a coordinate to 0 and the detector extent
get_detector_size returns the SensorWidth and SensorHeight pylon nodes in pixels
start_grabbing writes AcquisitionFrameRate when a rate is given and starts grabbing with GrabStrategy_LatestImageOnly; stop_grabbing calls StopGrabbing
check_attribute_names looks for ExposureTime, ExposureTimeAbs or ExposureTimeRaw and for Gain, GainRaw or GainAll
close closes and detaches the pylon camera
list_cameras enumerates the pylon devices from the transport-layer factory
The DAQ viewer writes an exposure setting to the pylon node as int(value * 1e3), milliseconds to microseconds
The DAQ viewer reads an exposure value from the pylon node in microseconds and multiplies it by 1e-3 for the GUI
The DAQ viewer reads the pylon node minimum and maximum with GetMin() and GetMax(), so the usable range is reported by the camera at run time
The DAQ viewer changes the ROI through set_roi with hstart, hend=hstart+width, vstart, vend=vstart+height and the two binning factors
The DAQ viewer calls setup_acquisition when the camera is initialised
The DAQ viewer starts grabbing with the configured frame rate or with None when the model has no frame-rate parameter
The README says the plugin handles gain, exposure and ROI and uses the pypylon library
The README names the acA640-120gm, acA1920-40gm and puA1600-60um models as those the plugin was tested with
The README says the config file names are pylon API feature names such as ExposureTime or GainRaw and that a config file is needed per camera model
